title: Meta Brings Code Review Auto-Approval More Mainstream with PyTorch GreenLight
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/uber-agent-spend-steady/en/headerimage/radar-header-1200x630-1795391031838.jpg"/><p>PyTorch now lets an AI reviewer approve pull requests from its own maintainers. GreenLight is an open-source take on RADAR, the system Meta uses to auto-land low-risk diffs after safety checks, a risk score and an LLM review. OpenAI, Anthropic and Sonar describe similar ways to automate approval while keeping humans on risky changes.</p> <i>By Andrew Hoblitzell</i>

title: Netflix Builds Quasar to Measure the Blast Radius of Library API Changes
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Netflix developed Quasar, an internal tool that combines semantic code indexing and API comparisons to identify downstream consumers affected by library changes. Using SCIP, Amazon S3, and Athena, it traces API references across repositories, helping maintainers assess migration impact and make informed release decisions. Netflix is also exploring agent-assisted consumer migrations.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Grafana Begins Its Biggest UI Refresh Since Version 7
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/grfana-ui-refresh/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795008225435.jpg"/><p>Grafana Labs has introduced the first phase of its biggest visual refresh since Grafana 7, bringing updated themes, more consistent interface components, and improved visual hierarchy to its observability platform.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: From Fan-Out to Fast: Sub-100ms API Design in Distributed Systems
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/sub-100ms-latency-distributed-systems/en/mediumimage/saranya-vedagiri-medium-1793800504577.jpeg"/><p>Saranya Vedagiri explains how to design resilient, low-latency distributed APIs under 100ms. Drawing on practical scale at eBay, she discusses hop-by-hop latency budgets, async fanout tradeoffs, thread pool sizing, caching, and circuit breakers. Learn actionable strategies to eliminate tail-latency bottlenecks and establish performance-first engineering practices.</p> <i>By Saranya Vedagiri</i>

title: Article: Engineering Reliable Telematics from Smartphone Sensors
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/engineering-reliable-smartphone-sensor-telematics/en/headerimage/engineering-reliable-smartphone-sensor-telematics-header-1795176941366.jpg"/><p>Smartphones make telematics more accessible by combining location, motion sensors, computing power, and connectivity in a single device. But the convenience comes with a trade-off: device placement varies, sampling behavior is managed by the mobile platform, and measurements have different timing and coordinate semantics. This article explores a six-stage architecture to address these challenges.</p> <i>By Praveen Kumar Gopalakrishnan</i>

title: Mozilla Partners with Mistral to Bring Open-Weight AI Models to Firefox Smart Window
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/mozilla-mistral-ai-smart-window/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795716059601.jpg"/><p>Mozilla has partnered with Mistral AI to offer Mistral Small 4, an open-weight model, in Firefox's Smart Window AI assistant, now in beta. It is recommended for users in France, the US and Canada. Users can choose among several models, and Mistral agreed to zero data retention. Beta feedback is mixed.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: How to Kill the Code Review
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/qcon-sf-26-kill-code-review/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795712695641.jpg"/><p>Ankit Jain of Aviator told QCon San Francisco 2026 that line-by-line code review is already fading, since most review comments concern knowledge sharing rather than defects and over 75% of PRs merge without human review. He proposed six layers: argue, capture, codify, prove, debate, own. His team merges four times more PRs, with about 40% fewer reverts.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Building a Production-Ready Culture and Skills through SRE-Based Training
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/SRE-based-training/en/headerimage/header-1795590551520.jpg"/><p>Training can act as a confidence engine, turning repeated behaviors into habits and culture.  We can tailor training programs that equip developers and operators with the skills to run their services in line with the organization’s maturity and growth, and apply SRE principles to the training itself.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

title: Presentation: Finetuning Your Embedding Model for Better Search: Learning from Agentic Search at Dell
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/fine-tune-enterprise-rag-embeddings/en/mediumimage/rachel-shalo-medium-1793801102883.jpeg"/><p>Rachel Shalom explains how Dell solved enterprise RAG retrieval failures on internal terminology by fine-tuning open-source embedding models. She discusses data prep with hard negatives, distributed InfoNCE loss training on H100 GPUs, automated hyperparameter tuning, and production evaluation using LLM-as-a-judge.</p> <i>By Rachel Shalom</i>

title: .NET MAUI 11 Makes CoreCLR the Default Runtime and Adds Incremental XAML Hot Reload
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/dotnet-maui-11-coreclr-hotreload/en/headerimage/header-1795560880894.jpg"/><p>Microsoft released .NET 11 with a .NET MAUI update focused on product quality. CoreCLR is now the default runtime on all platforms, and XAML gets incremental hot reload, implicit namespaces and faster resource dictionaries. The release also adds device test templates and passkey support, and raises the minimum Android and Apple platform versions.</p> <i>By Edin Kapić</i>

title: Mock Service Worker Releases v3.0 with ESM-Only Build, Socket-Based Interception and GraphQL Subs
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/mock-service-worker-v3/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795626212829.jpg"/><p>Mock Service Worker 3.0 is now ESM-only, requires Node.js 22 or later, and cuts package size from 416KB to 234KB. It adds GraphQL subscription support, protocol-specific entrypoints, and an experimental defineNetwork API. Node.js interception now works at the TCP and TLS level. Some users report test failures from newly intercepted OPTIONS preflight requests.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Recap of Microsoft Ignite 2026: Copilot as the Work OS and Agent Governance
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/microsoft-ignite-2026-recap/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795605995597.jpg"/><p>At Ignite 2026, Microsoft positioned Copilot as the operating system for work and extended agent identity, governance, and cost controls across Azure, Foundry, Entra, and Defender. Highlights include Cobalt 200 VMs, Azure HorizonDB, a continuous improvement loop in Foundry, Microsoft IQ, a standalone Azure AI Gateway, and Windows Server 2028.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 Aims to Make Robots Safer, More Dexterous, and Faster Learners
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/deepmind-gemini-robotics-2-5/en/headerimage/tripadvisor-tca-migration-1795623375360.jpeg"/><p>Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, a vision-language-action (VLA) model designed to improve robots' dexterity, reliability, and learning speed, while enabling safer operation in unstructured real-world environments.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: GitHub Ditches CSS-in-JS for CSS Modules, Reports 55% Faster SSR after Three-Year Migration
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/github-css-migration/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795537886697.jpg"/><p>GitHub migrated github.com from styled-components to CSS Modules over three years, reporting a 55% cut in server-side rendering time and 25% faster component initialisation. Primer components were converted behind feature flags, and about 7,760 sx prop usages were migrated with codemods and Copilot agents. Commenters questioned user impact and hashed class names.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: DoorDash Scales Dispatch 10x While Maintaining 99.99% Peak Availability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/doordash-dispatch-redesign/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793847001864.jpg"/><p>DoorDash has redesigned its real-time dispatch platform, replacing a monolithic optimization engine with a distributed architecture that separates coordination from computation. The new system delivers 10x higher throughput and more than 99.99% peak availability. It also supports hybrid machine learning inference and multi-agent reinforcement learning to dynamically optimize delivery assignments.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>
